Predicates:
Virus(x) ::: x is a virus.
Disease(x) ::: x is a disease.
CausedBy(x, y) ::: x is caused by y.
OccurIn(x, y) ::: x can occur in y.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
SymptomOf(x, y) ::: x is a symptom of y.
Fever(x) ::: x has a fever.
Tired(x) ::: x feels tired.
Coughing(x) ::: x has coughing.
Glu(x) ::: x gets a glu.
Premises:
Disease(monkeypox) ∧ Virus(monkeypoxVirus) ∧ CausedBy(monkeypox, monkeypoxVirus) ::: Monkeypox is an infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus.
OccurIn(monkeypoxVirus, certainAnimals) ∧ OccurIn(monkeypoxVirus, human) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals, including humans.
∀x (Human(x) → Mammal(x)) ::: Humans are mammals.
∀x (Mammal(x) → Animal(x)) ::: Mammals are animals.
SymptomOf(fever, monkeypox) ∧ SymptomOf(headache, monkeypox) ∧ Symptom
Of(musclePains, monkeypox) ∧ SymptomOf(tired, monkeypox) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, feeling tired, and so on.
∀x (Glu(x) → Tired(x)) ::: People feel tired when they get a glu.
Conclusion:
SymptomOf(coughing, monkeypox) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include coughing.
(Fever(x) ∧ Mammal(x)) → CausedBy(x, monkeypoxVirus) ::: If a person has a fever and is a mammal, then the person has Monkeypox.
OccurIn(monkeypoxVirus, mammal) ::: The monkeypox virus can occur in mammals.
